# Troubleshooting

Symptoms first, in the order people actually hit them. Every entry says what
the message means, not just what to type.

## Build and dependencies

### `error: no matching package named 'patala-core' found`

patala is not published. There is no crates.io release, no PyPI package and no
`go get` — `SECURITY.md` says so plainly, and it is why there is nothing to
sign or checksum yet. Depend on it by path or by git:

```toml
patala-core = { git = "https://github.com/vul-os/patala" }
```

### `cargo build` succeeds but a rail crate is missing

Expected. `patala-solana`, `patala-stellar` and `patala-hyperswitch` are
deliberately outside the workspace's `default-members`, so a plain
`cargo build`/`cargo test` at the root never builds them. Name them:

```bash
cargo build -p patala-solana
cargo test  -p patala-stellar
```

This is [the offline default build](offline-by-default.md) working, not
failing.

### A `patala-fiat` adapter type does not exist

`patala-fiat`'s default feature set is empty. `StripeRail` is behind the
`stripe` feature:

```toml
patala-fiat = { path = "../patala-fiat", features = ["stripe"] }
```

### `cargo test --workspace` passes but you changed a fiat adapter

`cargo test --workspace` builds every crate with its **default** features, and
`patala-fiat`'s default set is empty — so a plain workspace run executes the
currency table, the registry and the `manual` rail, and **none** of the twenty
adapters. That was hundreds of tests that existed and never ran.

Run the repo's actual gate, which is seven — `fmt-check`, `lint`, `test`,
`test-features`, `doc`, `features` and `site-check`:

```bash
make check
```

If you only want the feature-gated half:

```bash
make test-features   # cargo test -p patala-fiat --all-features
                     # cargo test -p patala-uniffi --features fiat-all
                     # cargo test -p patala-ffi  --features fiat-all
```

And if you want to check that **one** processor still builds alone, which is the
configuration an operator actually ships:

```bash
cargo build -p patala-fiat --features yoco
```

That is a gate now (`make features`, i.e. `scripts/check-features.sh`), and it
is new in 0.1.1 because until then fourteen of the twenty did not compile —
`--all-features` and the empty default set both did, so nothing noticed.

The same applies to clippy: `cargo clippy --workspace` lints each crate at its
default features, which for `patala-fiat` means twenty adapters never linted.
`make lint` runs it twice for that reason.

## Python

### `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'patala'`

The generated wrapper is build output, not a checked-in file, and it is not on
your path yet. Either build a wheel and install it —

```bash
cd patala-py && maturin build --release && pip install target/wheels/patala_py-*.whl
```

— or use the manual flow and point `PYTHONPATH` at the output directory:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=patala-py/bindings/python python3 your_script.py
```

### The import works but fails loading the native library

The generated `patala.py` loads its cdylib **by name, from its own
directory**. Generating the wrapper does not copy the library next to it —
step 3 of the manual flow does:

```bash
cp target/debug/libpatala_py.dylib patala-py/bindings/python/
#  (Linux: libpatala_py.so)
```

If you rebuilt the cdylib with different features, copy it again. A stale
library beside a fresh wrapper is the usual cause of "the constructor exists
in the wrapper but the symbol is missing".

### `AttributeError: type object 'PatalaRail' has no attribute 'new_fiat'`

The cdylib those bindings were generated from was built without the fiat
features, so that constructor does not exist in it. Rebuild and regenerate:

```bash
cargo build -p patala-py --features fiat-all      # or fiat-stripe, etc.
```

The same applies to `new_solana`, `new_stellar` and `new_hyperswitch`, each
behind its own feature.

### `PatalaError.InvalidRequest: unknown fiat provider "..."`

Either the name is genuinely wrong — it is matched case-insensitively — or
that provider's Cargo feature was not compiled into this build. Ask the build
what it has rather than guessing:

```python
from patala import patala_fiat_providers
print(patala_fiat_providers())
```

### `TypeError` on `PayRequest(...)` or `capabilities()._class`

`class` is a Python keyword, so the field is `_class`. Nothing else was
renamed. Amounts are `int` minor units — passing a float is a bug, not a
convenience.

## Go

### `build constraints exclude all Go files in .../bindings/patala`

`CGO_ENABLED=0`. The bindings are cgo and will not compile without it. This is
the exact failure the [cgo cost](go.md#the-cgo-cost) section describes, and it
is verified rather than assumed.

If your project needs `CGO_ENABLED=0` — a pure-static binary, easy
cross-compilation — that is a signal to use [the sidecar](sidecar.md) instead.
`cackle` made that call for these reasons.

### `ld: library not found for -lpatala_uniffi` / link errors

The cdylib is not built, or not on the linker's search path. Use the Makefile
rather than retyping the flags — it is the one place the filename and the
`CGO_LDFLAGS` live:

```bash
cd patala-go && make build
```

### The binary builds, then fails at startup on another machine

Expected, and documented. A cgo binary links dynamically against the cdylib,
and Rust's default dylib install name is the **build-time absolute path** —
`otool -L` shows it. Ship the library with the binary and set
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`/`DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`, or fix the install name with
`install_name_tool`/`-rpath`. A pure-Go static binary has none of this, which
is the whole trade.

### `undefined: patala.PatalaRailNewFiat`

Same cause as the Python version: the cdylib was built without the fiat
features. Regenerate:

```bash
cd patala-go && make FEATURES=fiat-all generate
```

And remember the Go side needs the build tag too — `go test -tags fiat`, or
the `make test-fiat` / `make run-example-fiat` targets, because Go has no
per-dependency optional-feature mechanism.

### `uniffi-bindgen-go` generation fails against the cdylib

Version mismatch. The generator is versioned against a specific `uniffi-rs`
release and must match this workspace's pin:

```bash
cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/NordSecurity/uniffi-bindgen-go \
    --tag v0.5.0+v0.29.5 uniffi-bindgen-go
```

Installing without `--tag` gets a build targeting a newer `uniffi-rs` than
this workspace pins.

### `go vet` reports `possible misuse of unsafe.Pointer`

Expected and benign, in generated FFI glue. It is the same class of note any
hand-rolled cgo binding produces.

## The language packages

The full set is in [Fifteen language packages](language-packages.md); these are
the four traps that cost real time to find.

### A `fork()`ed worker hangs — occasionally, and never in the test

The library is fork-safe. **A handle that is in use at the moment of the fork is
not.** Its runtime sits behind a mutex, and `fork()` copies a locked mutex as
locked, with nobody in the child to unlock it. The window is a few microseconds
wide, so most forks look fine: measured under a parent with four threads
charging on the same handle, an inherited handle hung **4–8 times in 200** and a
handle opened in the child hung **0 in 200**. Reproduced independently in Python
and Ruby.

**A test that forks once is a false green.** Fix it by opening the handle in the
child — Unicorn's `after_fork`, clustered Puma's `on_worker_boot`, Resque in the
job's child, or simply per request. Loading the *library* before the fork is
fine. Note also that the two in-process surfaces differ: the C ABI starts no
threads at all, while `patala-py`/`patala-go` bring up two Tokio workers on the
first call. MockRail survived a fork through the UniFFI path too, but only
because `block_on` drives on the calling thread and MockRail spawns nothing — a
rail doing real network I/O may want those workers, and that case is
**UNMEASURED**.

### PHP: `FFI API is restricted by "ffi.enable"` in an fpm worker

`ffi.enable` defaults to `preload`, and the manual's recommended production
shape — declare the ABI in an `opcache.preload` script, reach it from request
code with `FFI::scope()` — **does not work under php-fpm on PHP 8.5.9**. The
preload exemption is lifted for the **CLI SAPI only**, which is why the same
code runs happily from `php examples/direct_charge.php` and throws in a worker.
Set `ffi.enable=1`, or use the sidecar.

The second half of the trap: `ffi.enable` and `opcache.preload` are
`PHP_INI_SYSTEM`, so a `php_admin_value` in a pool block is applied *per worker,
after the fork* and silently does nothing for either. Set them in `php.ini`.

### Elixir: the sidecar keeps serving after `Port.close/1`

`Port.close/1` closes the port, not the OS process. The child keeps running with
its stdin at EOF, still bound to its port, and the next `spawn` picks a
different one while the old server answers requests nobody meant to send. Call
`Patala.Sidecar.stop/1`, which terminates the child rather than just dropping
the pipe.

### Elixir: `dlopen` fails with an empty error message

Almost certainly a zero-byte `.so`, and it reads like a linker fault for as long
as it takes to run `ls -la priv/`. Mix normally **symlinks** `_build/<env>/lib/patala/priv`
at the source `priv/`, so a build step that copies a NIF into `priv/` copies a
file onto itself through the symlink — `File.cp!` truncates it to 0 bytes.
Rebuild the NIF rather than copying it.

## Sidecar

### It exits immediately with an `export` line printed

Working as designed. The server refuses to start without
`PATALA_SIDECAR_TOKEN`. There is no auto-generated fallback and no
unauthenticated-by-default path; it prints the command you need and exits `1`.

```bash
export PATALA_SIDECAR_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
```

### `401` on every request

The token is missing, malformed, or wrong. All three are the same `401` with
no distinguishing detail, deliberately. Every `/v1/...` route needs
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` — including the read-only capabilities lookup,
not just the money-moving ones. `/healthz` is the only unauthenticated route.

### `404` for a rail that definitely exists in the repo

**The sidecar's registry is mock-only.** `default_registry()` has exactly one
entry, `"mock"`. Solana, Stellar, Hyperswitch and the fiat adapters are not
reachable through the sidecar today; the per-rail registration is unwritten
work. A `registry_is_mock_only` test pins that so this cannot quietly become
untrue in either direction. See [Status](status.md).

### I cannot make it listen on `0.0.0.0`

You cannot, and that is not a missing feature. The bind address is hardcoded
to `127.0.0.1`; only the port is configurable. A sidecar that could be told to
listen off-box would turn "local key isolation" into "network-exposed payment
API with a bearer token", which is a much worse posture. There is also no TLS,
for the same reason there is no network hop to protect on loopback.

### `200` came back — did the payment work?

Not necessarily, and this is the most important thing to get right about this
API. A `200` means **the rail answered**. `/verify` returns `200` with
`{"valid": false}`; `/validate-destination` returns `200` for all five
verdicts including the refusals. Read the body, and branch on `status` and
`is_refusal`. See [The sidecar HTTP API](sidecar.md).

## Payments and verification

### `charge()` returned `Ok` but nothing settled

Correct behaviour, on several rails. A charge awaiting the buyer comes back
with `amount_minor: 0`. **Gate entitlement on `verify` returning `true`,
never on `charge` returning `Ok`.** `verify` re-derives the answer from the
rail; `charge` only means the request was accepted.

### `verify()` returns `false` and I expected `true`

`false` is the fail-closed *answer*, not an error, and it is returned on any
doubt: wrong rail, malformed proof, unsettled status, amount or currency
mismatch, tampered receipt. Check that the receipt you stored is the one you
are passing back, byte for byte — the binding covers the reference and
destination precisely so an edited field stops verifying.

An `Err`, by contrast, means the check **could not be performed** — an
operational failure. Never read it as "probably not settled".

### `refund()` returns `Unsupported` on a crypto rail

Permanent and intentional. Finality is the whole point of
`NonCustodialFinal`, and faking a reversal would flatten the distinction
`RailClass` exists to preserve. Paying the customer back is a *second*
payment, to an address the **customer** supplies — never the address the
payment came from, which is very often an exchange withdrawal address where
the funds cannot be credited back to them. The whole flow, including the
wording to show a customer, is in
[Paying a customer back](compensating-payments.md).

On a fiat rail, which is `CustodialReversible`, `refund` is the right call and
no destination is involved. A few processors have no refund API; those return
`Unsupported` and the refund happens in the processor's dashboard.

### `validate_destination` returned `Unknown` and I expected a check

On a fiat rail that is the honest ceiling, not a gap. `destination` there is a
redirect URL, a buyer email, or a string the rail never reads — none of them a
place money goes. Claiming `StructurallyValid` would tell you a `success_url`
had been vetted as somewhere to send a customer's money.

**Never treat `Unknown` as valid**, and never as a refusal either: "checked
and clean" and "could not check" are different answers.

### `Error::CrossClassFailover`

A `FailoverRail` refused to fall from a `NonCustodialFinal` request onto a
`CustodialReversible` rail, or the reverse. That changes the guarantee you
handed the payer, so it is opt-in:

```rust
let rail = FailoverRail::new(rails).allow_cross_class(true);
```

Do that only if you mean it.

### A webhook does not verify, and the signature looks right

Almost always the body. Every scheme signs the **exact bytes** the processor
sent, so a body that has been through a JSON round trip on your side will not
verify. Pass the raw bytes you read off the request, before any decoding, and
forward the headers and — for LNbits, which puts its secret in the URL — the
query string too.

**Through the sidecar, three headers are dropped before the rail sees them**:
`authorization`, `proxy-authorization` and `cookie`, plus any header whose value
is not valid UTF-8. Since 0.1.1. No scheme in this workspace reads any of those
names, and the sidecar's own bearer token travels in `Authorization` — see
[the sidecar](sidecar.md#three-headers-are-dropped-since-011). The body is still
byte for byte.

### A webhook verified, with status `Unconfirmed`

The delivery is genuine and says **nothing about money**. BTCPay, Coinbase
Commerce, OpenNode and LNbits all authenticate a notification that names an
object and nothing else. (Mollie does not belong in that list and never did: it
re-fetches from the processor, as iyzico, mercadopago, payfast and paypal do,
and returns a real settlement verdict.) Look up your stored receipt for
`event.object_id` and call `verify` on it. Never treat `Unconfirmed` as
payment — it is not `NotSettled` either, and reporting it as one would be a
lie in the other direction.
